content:
# 1 Maccabees Chapter 2 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, 1 Maccabees 2 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/1MA_002_page_001.jpg

---

1. In those days there was a priest named Mattathias, son of John, son of Simeon, of the priestly division of Joarib. He had left Jerusalem and settled in Modein.
2. He had five sons: John, known as Gaddi;
3. Simon, known as Thassi;
4. Judas, who was called Maccabeus;
5. Eleazar, known as Avaran; and Jonathan, known as Apphus.
6. When he saw what was being done — the blasphemies spreading through Judah and Jerusalem —
7. he cried out: "Why was I born to watch this? My people are being destroyed. The holy city is ruined. I live to see her handed over to her enemies, the sanctuary given to foreigners.
8. Her temple is like a man stripped of all dignity.
9. Her treasures have been carted off into exile. Her children are butchered in her streets. Her young men fall to enemy swords.
10. Every nation has helped itself to her palace and grabbed its share of the plunder.
11. Everything beautiful about her has been taken away. She was free — now she is a slave.
12. Look at it: our sacred things, our beauty, our glory — all of it ruined. The Gentiles have fouled it all.
13. What reason is there left to live?"
14. Mattathias and his sons tore their clothes, put on sackcloth, and wept without restraint.
15. Then the king's enforcers arrived in Modein to force the people to sacrifice. They had been going from town to town across Judah.
16. A crowd of Israelites gathered around them. Mattathias and his sons were there too.
17. The king's officers turned to Mattathias: "You are a leader here — a man of standing, powerful, respected, surrounded by sons and brothers.
18. Be the first to step forward. Do what the king commands. Every nation has done it. The Jews in Jerusalem have done it. Do it, and you and your family will be counted among the king's friends. You will be rewarded with silver and gold and fine gifts."
19. Mattathias shouted his answer for everyone to hear: "Even if every nation under the king's rule bows down to him and every man abandons the faith of his fathers to do what the king wants —
20. I will not. My sons will not. My brothers will not. We will walk in the covenant of our fathers.
21. God forbid we should ever abandon the Torah and its commandments.
22. We will not obey the king. We will not turn from our worship — not one step to the right, not one step to the left."
23. The moment he finished speaking, a Jewish man walked up — in full view of everyone — and sacrificed on the altar in Modein, doing exactly what the king had commanded.
24. The sight of it hit Mattathias like a blow. Zeal blazed up inside him, burning in his gut. He ran forward and cut the man down right there on the altar.
25. In the same motion he killed the king's officer who had been enforcing the sacrifice, and he tore down the altar.
26. His zeal for the Torah was the same zeal that Phinehas had shown against Zimri son of Salu.
27. Mattathias stood in the middle of the town and bellowed: "Anyone who is on fire for the Torah, anyone who holds to the covenant — come with me!"
28. He and his sons abandoned everything they owned in the city and fled to the hills.
29. Many others followed — men who were hungry for justice and righteousness — heading into the wilderness to take shelter there:
30. themselves, their wives and children, and their animals, because the evil bearing down on them had become unbearable.
31. Reports reached the king's officers and the garrison in Jerusalem, the city of David, that men who had defied the king's decree had fled into hiding in the wilderness.
32. A large force went after them and caught up with them. They made camp facing them and got ready to attack — it was the sabbath.
33. "Come out now," they called. "Do what the king says and you will live."
34. "We will not come out," the people answered. "We will not do what the king says. We will not profane the sabbath day."
35. The soldiers launched their assault at once.
36. The Jews made no move to resist. They did not throw a single stone. They did not seal the cave entrances.
37. They only said: "We die with clean hands. Heaven and earth are witness — you are murdering innocent people."
38. The attack came on the sabbath, and they were killed — men, women, children, livestock — about a thousand souls.
39. When Mattathias and his companions heard what had happened, they were devastated.
40. They said to one another: "If we all do what our brothers did and refuse to fight back — even to save our own lives and our religion — these people will finish us off quickly. There will be nothing left."
41. That day they made a ruling: "If anyone attacks us on the sabbath, we fight back. We will not die like our brothers died, hiding in those caves."
42. Around this time the Hasideans joined them — fierce fighters in Israel, men who had given themselves completely to the Torah.
43. All the fugitives from the persecutions swelled the ranks, reinforcing them.
44. They built an army. They struck down sinners with fury and lawless men with rage. The survivors scattered to the Gentiles.
45. Mattathias and his men swept through the country, pulling down pagan altars wherever they found them.
46. They forcibly circumcised every uncircumcised boy they found within Israel's territory.
47. They hounded the arrogant and pressed forward, and the work went well.
48. They wrested the Torah out of Gentile hands, out of the grasp of kings. They never gave the sinner the advantage.
49. When Mattathias felt death coming on, he called his sons together and said: "Arrogance has triumphed. Contempt has grown powerful. This is a time of catastrophe and blazing anger.
50. My sons — burn for the Torah. Lay down your lives for the covenant of our fathers.
51. Remember what our ancestors did in their day. Win for yourselves honor and an everlasting name.
52. Abraham was tested — and wasn't he found faithful? It was credited to him as righteousness.
53. Joseph was in terrible trouble — and he kept the commandment. He ended up ruling Egypt.
54. Phinehas our ancestor burned with zeal — and he received the covenant of an everlasting priesthood.
55. Joshua did everything he was commanded — and he became a judge in Israel.
56. Caleb spoke up truly in the assembly — and he received his portion in the land.
57. David showed faithfulness and compassion — and he inherited the throne of the kingdom forever.
58. Elijah burned with zeal for the Torah — and he was taken up into heaven.
59. Hananiah, Azariah, and Mishael trusted God — and they were saved from the furnace.
60. Daniel had integrity — and he was delivered from the lions.
61. Think about this, generation after generation: everyone who trusts in God will not be abandoned.
62. Don't be afraid of a sinful man's threats. His glory is dung and worms.
63. He stands high today and tomorrow he's gone — returned to the dust, his schemes turned to nothing.
64. My sons: be strong, be brave, be rooted in the Torah. Through it, you will be glorified.
65. Listen to me about Simon. He is a man of wisdom. Obey him all your days. He will be a father to you.
66. And Judas Maccabeus — he has been strong as iron since he was young. Make him your war commander. Lead the people's fight.
67. Gather every Torah-keeper around you and take vengeance for your people.
68. Give the Gentiles what they have coming. Keep the commandments of the Torah."
69. Then he blessed them, and he was gathered to his ancestors.
70. He died in the one hundred and forty-sixth year. His sons buried him in the family tomb at Modein, and all Israel wept for him with great mourning.
